theme: 宠物-工作犬野外走失事件

content.text: Shiyan, emergency! My dog Lightning chased a marmot into the rolling terrain while we were shooting on the plateau meadow and has been missing for over two hours. This is his photo. I'm going crazy with worry.
Ye Lu, don't panic just yet. Take a deep breath. Safety first, let's proceed step by step. Is Lightning wearing a collar? Does it have a tag or contact information on it?

Wearing a black collar with my phone number on the tag. But the signal here is intermittent, and I'm worried it might run too far to be reached. Just like the valley signal issue we discussed when planning for emergencies.
Good, where there's a nameplate, there's hope. Now, describe the specific terrain around the last place you saw it—are there any ditches, caves, or rivers?

This is the surrounding environment of the final location: an open meadow with fences in the distance, but the terrain is undulating and may conceal low-lying areas. There are no obvious rivers, but I’ve heard there are seasonal streams nearby.

Received. This type of small dog typically doesn't run too far in unfamiliar open areas, but be cautious of birds of prey and weather changes. Immediately place an item with your scent, such as the jacket you're wearing, at the last known location.
Okay, I'll release it now. But it's windy here, so how long will the scent linger? Should I proceed cautiously, like we confirmed before we set out?

Yes, stability is more important than speed. After setting down your equipment, find a nearby high point and use your telephoto lens or binoculars to observe. Lightning is conspicuous in color and should be easy to spot against a green background.

I'll give it a try, but the terrain is uneven and the visibility is limited. By the way, how is your old knee injury? Don't let my situation affect your recovery, just like the long-term management we discussed in Session 7.

I'm fine, the usual soreness has lessened a lot, thanks to your previous recovery plan. Now focusing on Lightning: Are there any herders or reserve staff nearby? Team collaboration can expand the search area.
There's a herder's tent a few kilometers away where I can go for help. But Lightning is timid and might hide if strangers approach. Should I bring some of his favorite food?

Good idea, bring food and its familiar toys. At the same time, set a search boundary: prioritize a radius of 500 meters centered on the last known location to avoid expanding blindly. Your previous hiking and orienteering skills will come in handy now.

Understood. I'll use a compass and map to delineate the area, just like how we optimize routes during in-depth planning. But the longer it takes, the more worried I become. Lightning is only three years old and lacks experience in the wilderness.

Stay calm, observation is key. I'll send a picture to illustrate: scan systematically from high ground, paying attention to shadows and dense vegetation. Lightning might curl up out of fear, so patience is needed.
I see the picture. I'll observe it as attentively as you do. Also, the weather report says there might be thunderstorms in the evening. Should I set a withdrawal time as agreed in the emergency plan?

Yes, safety first. Set a two-hour limit. If we don’t find it, return to the safe point first, contact the herders for assistance, and resume the search tomorrow. Respect nature and avoid putting yourself at risk.

Alright, I'll follow your advice. From Session 1 until now, your professional guidance has always put me at ease. This time, I'll proceed in an organized manner: first, I'll place the scented items, then observe and seek help if needed.

Exactly. Remember, Lightning's adaptability might exceed expectations, just like your performance when filming in the valley. Keep communication open, and let me know if anything comes up. I'll provide remote support.
Thank you, Shiyan! I've shifted from panic to action. Starting now, and I'll keep you updated. Your calmness is always a reassuring anchor in critical moments.
Go ahead, stay safe. Work together as a team, including you and Lightning. Waiting for your good news.
